docs_facts.fact: Client tools (your own, plus bash/text_editor/memory/computer use) run in your app: Claude returns stop_reason tool_use with tool_use blocks, you reply with a tool_result block carrying the matching tool_use_id. Server tools (web_search, web_fetch, code_execution, tool_search) run on Anthropic's side. A custom tool is name, description, input_schema; strict: true guarantees schema-valid inputs. Tool definitions and tool blocks all count as input tokens, plus a per-model tool-use system prompt overhead (e.g. 286 tokens on Opus 5.5 with auto/none).

Request field controlling tool calling. Default {type: auto} lets Claude decide; values auto, none, any and tool appear in the docs (the pricing table keys on auto/none versus any/tool). auto accepts disable_parallel_tool_use: true to cap Claude at one tool call per turn. Exact semantics of any and tool and their interaction with thinking: not verified (define-tools page not fetched).

The tool value is listed as a tool_choice option (it, like any, costs more tool-use system-prompt tokens than auto/none). That it forces one named tool is not stated on the fetched page: not verified.
Default. Claude decides per turn whether to call a tool or answer directly. Can be steered with system-prompt wording; combine with disable_parallel_tool_use: true for at most one tool call per turn.

Seven values: end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn (server-tool loop hit its default 10-iteration limit; resend the assistant content to continue), refusal (HTTP 200, read stop_details, can retry on a fallback model), model_context_window_exceeded (response filled the context window; treat as truncated). A client tool_use never yields pause_turn.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: refusal and model_context_window_exceeded are newer values; older lists name only the first four.

docs_facts.fact: Request parameter capping output tokens; hitting it ends the response with stop_reason max_tokens, so raise it or continue the response. Sync output max is 128K tokens on the current models; Batches API can reach 300k with beta header output-300k-2026-03-24. Each batched request needs max_tokens of at least 1.

Server-side tool letting Claude discover tools on demand. Two variants: tool_search_tool_regex_20251119 (Claude writes Python regex, 200-char cap) and tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119 (natural language, 500-char cap). Put the full definition of every tool in tools; mark the ones to hide with defer_loading: true; at least one tool (not the search tool) must stay non-deferred, else 400. Up to 10,000 deferred tools; 5 results by default (limit 1-10,000). Preserves prompt caching; a deferred tool cannot carry cache_control. Not metered separately.

Blocks of type tool_reference returned inside the search result pointing at discovered tools by tool_name; the API expands them to full definitions server-side. Custom client-side search can also return tool_reference blocks inside a normal tool_result, and each must have a matching definition in top-level tools. Never return a tool_result for a srvtoolu_ id.
The overview shows tool_result content as a plain string or content blocks. A specific recommendation about JSON-encoding tool results: not verified.

The stop-reason page says a refusal can be retried on a fallback model and links a refusals-and-fallback page (not fetched). Claude Code separately has --fallback-model / fallbackModel for overloaded or retired models. What 'server-side fallback' specifically denotes: not verified.

Cache prompt prefixes via cache_control. Automatic caching: one top-level cache_control that moves its breakpoint forward. Explicit breakpoints on blocks: up to 4 per request; lookback window 20 blocks. TTL 5 minutes default, 1 hour at 2x base input write price. Reads cost a fraction of base (Opus 5.5 $0.20 vs $4 base per MTok; Sonnet 5.5 $0.10 vs $2). Minimum cacheable prompt is 512 tokens on Fable 5.1/Opus 5.5/Sonnet 5.5/Haiku 5.5, 1,024 on Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5/4.6, 4,096 on Opus 4.6/4.5 and Haiku 4.5; shorter prompts silently skip caching. Check cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens (both 0 means not cached); input_tokens counts only tokens after the last breakpoint. Caches are isolated per workspace on the Claude API.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Minimum cacheable length differs sharply by model generation; older tables show 1,024/2,048 for everything.

docs_facts.fact: Marker object, shape {type: ephemeral, ttl: 5m|1h}, placed on a content block (explicit breakpoint) or at the request top level (automatic caching). Put it on the last block whose prefix is identical across requests; marking content that changes every request pays cache writes and never reads. With 4 explicit breakpoints already, a top-level one returns 400. Changing any earlier block invalidates later cache entries.

Asynchronous bulk Messages at a 50% discount. POST /v1/messages/batches with requests each carrying custom_id (1-64 chars, alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore) and params. Limits: 100,000 requests or 256 MB per batch; most finish within 1 hour, expire after 24 hours; results downloadable for 29 days via results_url. processing_status goes in_progress to ended; request_counts has succeeded, errored, canceled, expired. Results can return in any order, so match by custom_id. Prompt-cache hits are best-effort.

POST /v1/messages/count_tokens takes the same inputs as message creation (system, tools, images, PDFs, thinking) and returns input_tokens. The count is an estimate and can differ slightly from actual usage. Free to use but rate limited per usage tier.

Current lineup per the overview page: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1; demanding reasoning, long-horizon agentic work, $10/$50 per MTok), Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5; agentic coding and knowledge work, $4/$20), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5; speed/intelligence balance, $2/$10), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5; high-volume low-latency, from $0.10/$0.50). All: 1M context, 128K max output, adaptive thinking, knowledge cutoff Jun 2026. Default effort: high (Fable, Sonnet) or medium (Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5). Mythos models appear on other pages as limited-availability. Legacy still available: claude-fable-5, claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8, claude-opus-4-7, claude-opus-4-6, claude-opus-4-5-20251101, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: A fourth top tier (Fable) and the 5.5 generation exist; exam items built around 4.x Opus/Sonnet/Haiku name legacy models. Dateless IDs from the 4.6 generation on are themselves pinned snapshots.

docs_facts.fact: Legacy but Active; ID claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. Earliest possible retirement on the Anthropic-operated platforms: not sooner than October 15, 2026 (no deprecation notice yet in the table). Recommended replacement target in older deprecations was this model; Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) is the current Haiku. Minimum cacheable prompt 4,096 tokens.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Retirement floor of Oct 15, 2026 is already passed as of 2026-10-28 while the table still shows Active; watch for a deprecation notice.

docs_facts.fact: Legacy but Active; ID claude-opus-4-8; not sooner than May 28, 2027. It is now the replacement target named for retired Opus 4 / 4.1 / Opus 3 in the deprecations history. 1,024-token minimum for caching; supports tool search and structured outputs.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Newer Opus (5, 5.5) exist; questions treating Opus 4.8 as newest are stale.

docs_facts.fact: Lifecycle states: Active, Legacy, Deprecated, Retired. At least 60 days notice for publicly released models. Deprecated now: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (deprecated 2026-09-30, retires 2026-11-30, replacement claude-sonnet-5-5); claude-mythos-preview deprecated 2026-06-09. Retired: claude-opus-4-1-20250805 (2026-08-05), claude-opus-4-20250514 and claude-sonnet-4-20250514 (2026-06-15), claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219 and claude-3-5-haiku-20241022 (2026-02-19), claude-3-haiku-20240307 (2026-04-20). Parameter deprecation: temperature, top_p, top_k removed in API version 2026-10-21 (400 even at default). Bedrock and Google-managed set their own dates.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Sonnet 4.5 retires 2026-11-30 (30 days from today); sampling-parameter removal landed 2026-10-21.

docs_facts.fact: Set via output_config.effort. Level names seen in the Claude Code docs: low, medium, high, xhigh, max (the effort page excerpt read here showed medium and max explicitly). Default is high on most models; Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium (per this page; the models overview shows Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5 as high). Passing the model's default is identical to omitting it. max is available on the Fable/Mythos models and Opus 5.5/5/4.8 among others. Thinking is adaptive on current models; manual budget_tokens extended thinking is not accepted on later models.
docs_facts.exam_era_risk: Extended thinking with budget_tokens is deprecated on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 and rejected on later models; effort plus adaptive thinking replaces it.
